Thiis says quite a lot about current market sentiment as investors are so focused on finding reasons to sell the AI trade that they are overlooking what is happening underneath.

Anthropic is approaching operating break-even, revenue growth is accelerating, and the company is already generating more revenue than its reported compute costs.

Hock Tan was running out of patience.

The CEO of chip maker Broadcom had spent nearly two months trying to get banks to commit over $40 billion to the largest artificial-intelligence debt deal ever. It was meant to allow Anthropic to lease specialized chips that Broadcom is developing with Google.

Though Anthropic was the main beneficiary of the deal, the startup needed help from its bigger commercial partners to raise the money. Together, Anthropic and Broadcom were trying to close the deal ahead of Anthropic’s filing for its widely anticipated initial public offering.

Broadcom, the supplier of chips to Anthropic, was at the center of the action. Thanks to its sterling credit rating, it had already agreed to provide some financial guarantees to make banks more comfortable with the sizable risk of lending over $40 billion. But over the past few weeks, some of the banks grew increasingly anxious about participating in the deal, known as “Project North Star,” people familiar with the matter said.

Given the rise in interest rates and growing difficulties in the markets for artificial intelligence ventures, some banks felt they weren’t being compensated enough to take the risk and considered pulling out altogether, the people said.
In the end, Broadcom’s CEO held 11th-hour talks with bank executives over the weekend to get them to finalize their commitment to the deal and also agreed to higher interest rates on the loans, the people familiar with the matter said.

How could AI Infrastructure even collapse if Robotics Would Print Near Infinite GDP?

Most clear cut input and output tasks are very functional from financial modeling, software development, and capable of generating highly efficient machine learning solutions to complex queries.

This alone will be a multi trillion dollar industry.

But robotics will need even more compute due to video data being exponentially more sized data to train on. With robotics being the only way to grow out from the unsustainable triple digit deficit, along with it being a genuinely largest TAM possible in solving a labor shortage, it is practically inconceivable that AI compute will not be in extreme demand.

With robotics being possibly the biggest market of all time, solving issues like transportation and manual labor, the economy could quickly become deflationary. This will first roll out from teleoperated robots that will capture video footage from operators operating through VR sets, and has already been shown today in robotics training.

Moreover, compute is practically entirely constrained by TSMC’s capacity, as the ability to produce chips at a high yield is possibly the most complex industrial process ever developed. This means each unit of compute from TSMC is strategically vital to strategically attack competitors from acquiring that compute.

In this sense, compute is essentially an inelastic supply because the future payoff leads to monopolization of the biggest technology labor disruptor in human history.
In just a few years away in the 2030’s we could see mass production of robotics and an even bigger industrial boom than all others combined. Companies that capitalize on AI/robotics and compute/memory/photonics stocks are primed to go through an exponential growth that will eventually disrupt human labor the same way that hiring in technology has been disrupted.

TLDR: The payoff from multimodal AI and subsequent robotics AI will be the greatest opportunity for GDP capture in human history. Each unit of compute that goes to a competitor is a strategic failure. If GDP scales with units of compute, then computing is vastly undervalued currently with some of the largest known AI infrastructure names currently available between 5-20 forward PE.
